name: safari
title: Safari clone
description: A browser that only browses through your tailnet. Opening it shows a gate: nothing works until Tailscale is connected (a saved session is restored without a prompt; signing out brings the gate back), and behind it the browser is inert. Then a tabbed Safari: back and forward with per-tab history, an address field with suggestions from your tailnet's devices and your history, reload and stop, a tab strip and a tab overview, a start page of your devices with a Tailscale report, and a popover (TailscaleMenu) to see or end the connection and choose the exit node. Every page, stylesheet, image and form is fetched by the page itself through tailscale.fetch, which never falls back to the public network, and shown as a sealed document: scripts, frames, plug-ins and media removed, assets inlined as data URLs, and the frame under a Content-Security-Policy that forbids any request of its own, so a page cannot reach out around the tailnet. It is a document browser, not an app runtime. It uses the real Tailscale by default: Tailscale's own client as WebAssembly and its real sign-in page. A tailnet alone reaches your devices; for the public internet an exit node carries the traffic and the DNS lookups, and Safari picks one for you: opening a public address with none set selects the best online exit node (the one used last, else the first by name) and loads the page. The shield menu (TailscaleMenu) changes or clears it; choosing None is remembered, so a public address then explains why it fails, and Try Again turns an exit node back on (it also swaps an offline or failing exit node for another online one). With no online exit node it fails with an explanation. A simulated tailnet (data.ts) is there for stories and tests, never the default. Composed from TailscaleProvider, TailscaleMenu, TailscaleLoginButton, Button, Popover, Spinner, Icon and BLProvider.
